title: セイバールート十一日目-16

pages.ja:
公園は相変わらず無人だった。
今日がいつもより冷え込んでいる、という事もあるのだろう。
あたりに人気はなく、出歩いている人間は自分ぐらいのものだった。

pages.en:
The park is deserted, as always.

Perhaps the sharper cold today has something to do with it.

There is no one else around. I seem to be the only person foolish enough to venture outside.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The park is empty as usual.
Maybe it helps that it’s colder today than usual.
There is no one around and it looks like I’m the only one out at this time.

Now that I am here, I have to decide which path to take.

pages.en:
I cannot put the decision off any longer.

If we mean to defeat the remaining Masters and bring the Holy Grail War to an end, Saber must remain with us.

No. That has nothing to do with it. I simply do not want Saber to disappear.

But keeping her here would mean——

Making Saber attack people, just as Rider did.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There are no choices that allow me to postpone the problem.
If I am to end the Holy Grail War by defeating other Masters, I need Saber to stay.
No, even without that, I don’t want her to disappear.
But that means…
Having Saber attack people, like Rider did.

If I use one, I can force Saber to carry out my order no matter how fiercely she refuses.

Just as the cold finally sets my fingertips trembling——

I don’t know how long I remained slumped on this bench.
But just as my fingers start to tremble from the cold…

“Ah!

“There you are! I wondered where you had gone!”

Someone calls out to me without warning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh!

I’m suddenly called.

pages.mirrorMoon: “Aha, it is you. Hello, Shirou. You have a serious expression. What’s wrong?”

」

俺が心配する事でもないし、そもそも俺たちは敵同士ではなかったか。

I stop before I can finish and marvel at my own foolishness.

Illya is a Master too.

She has no need of my concern. More importantly, aren't the two of us enemies?
pages.mirrorMoon:
As I start to say that, I’m amazed at my stupidity.
Illya is a Master too.
I shouldn’t be worrying about this, and anyway, aren’t we enemies?

pages.ja: 「……悪い。今はイリヤと話をする余裕がないんだ。せっかく会えたけど、話し相手になってやれない。今日は冷えるし、帰ったほうがいいぞ」

pages.mirrorMoon: “…Sorry. I can’t afford to talk to you right now. We were lucky to see each other, but I can’t talk with you. It’s going to get cold today, so you should go home.”

pages.en:
Without rising from the bench, I turn Illya away.

…There is much more I need to discuss with this girl, but for now my mind is full of Saber.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Sitting down on the bench, I dismiss Illya.

“I know. Saber is about to disappear, isn't she?

“And Shirou is wondering what he should do about it.”

Without warning——

The girl before me speaks with a coldness that makes her seem like someone else.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I know. Saber’s going to disappear, right?
And you’re wondering what to do.”
Suddenly.
The girl in front of me says this coldly as if she is someone else.

“Illya…?”

“It's stupid to agonize over something like that. Rider's Master escaped because you're like this, Shirou. All you had to do was kill him once he lost.”

Some instinct tells me it is dangerous to remain seated, and I brace myself to rise.

“I'm glad I found you before anyone else could kill you.

pages.mirrorMoon:

…How long do I lie in perfect darkness?

Before I can decide whether I am alive or dead, my consciousness finally snaps away as well.

…How long has it been since I fell into this darkness?
While I wonder whether or not I’m dead, my consciousness fades away.

Though my mind has fallen into darkness, the fever in my flesh persists in declaring that I am alive.

I see. I guess I’m alive, then.

…She is absolutely right.

Without Saber, I cannot fight properly.

The Holy Grail War is a battle between Servants.

I could never hope to confront one of them myself.

That fact has been proven to me again and again.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…She’s right.
I can’t fight at all without Saber.
The Holy Grail War is a battle between Servants.
I cannot possibly match one of those Servants.
That fact has been proven many times already.

pages.ja:
滅多刺しだった。
セイバーの言う通り、俺にとってサーヴァントと戦うという事は、いかに生き延びるかという事だ。
それさえ俺は出来なかった。
体中切り刻まれ、あげくに三階から地上にたたき落とされたのだ。
命が助かったのは、自分でも判らない体の異常のおかげだろう。

pages.en:
I was cut to ribbons.

Just as Saber said, for me, fighting a Servant amounts to nothing more than struggling to survive.

I could not even manage that.

My body was carved apart, and finally I was hurled from the third floor to the ground.

I survived only because of some abnormality within my body that even I do not understand.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It was a merciless beating.
As Saber said, my battle against a Servant is to survive.
I couldn’t even do that.
I was cut all over my body, and on top of that, thrown to the ground from a third floor window.
I only survived because of an abnormality in my body that I don’t even understand.

pages.ja:
それが、怒りを覚えるほど悔しかった。
どんなに敵わない相手だからといって、目の前の惨事を止められなかった。
戦うと決めたのに。
マスターとして戦って、誰も傷つけないようにと決めたのに、守れなかった。

pages.en:
The memory frustrates me enough to kindle anger.

No matter how far the enemy surpassed me, I failed to stop the horror taking place before my eyes.

I had decided to fight.

Decided that I would enter this war as a Master and prevent anyone from being hurt—yet I protected no one.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That fact is so vexing that it makes me mad.
I could not stop the disaster occurring around me just because the one in front of me was unbeatable.
Even though I chose to fight,
I chose to fight as a Master to stop people getting hurt, but I could not protect them.

pages.ja:
頭にくる。
幼い頃から憧れていた正義の味方ってのは、いつだって勝たなければ意味がない。
pages.jaRuby:
頭にくる。
幼い頃から憧れていた正義の味方ってのは、いつだって勝たなければ意味がない。
pages.en:
—It infuriates me.

The Hero of Justice I have admired since childhood means nothing unless he finds a way to win every time.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It pisses me off.
The superhero I’ve admired since childhood always has to win or it’s meaningless.

pages.ja:
………体が熱い。
勝たなければいけない、と全身が震えている。
だが自分には勝つ手段はおろか、戦う手段さえない。
どうすればこの身だけで戦えるのか。
セイバーに負担をかけず、彼女を助けながら戦うだけの技量が自分には無い。

pages.en:
………My body is hot.

Every part of me trembles with the need to win.

Yet I possess no means of victory—no means even to fight.

How can I fight with this body alone?

I lack the skill to fight beside Saber and help her without becoming a burden.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…My body is burning.
My whole body is demanding that I must win.
But I don’t have any means of winning nor a way to fight.
How would I be able to fight?
I don’t have the skills to fight alongside Saber without being a burden to her.

それも間違いだ。衛宮士郎は格闘には向かない。
おまえの戦いは精神の戦い、
己との戦いであるべきだからだ

—That too is mistaken. Shirou Emiya is not made for physical combat.

Your battle should be one of the mind——

A battle against yourself——
pages.mirrorMoon:
That is a mistake as well. Emiya Shirou is not fit for fighting.
Because your fight is supposed to be a mental fight,
A fight with your own self

Suddenly——

I remember the back of the man who spoke those words.

判っている。
それは嫌というほど思い知らされた。
pages.jaRuby:
判っている。

pages.en:
I know.

That truth has been beaten into me more times than I care to remember.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I know.
I realize that more than ever now.

pages.ja:
ならば、せめてイメージしろ。
現実で敵わない相手なら、想像の中で勝て。
自身が勝てないのなら、勝てるモノを幻想しろ。
pages.jaRuby:
ならば、せめてイメージしろ。

pages.en:
—Then at least picture it.

If an enemy is beyond you in reality, defeat him in your imagination.

If you cannot win, then imagine something that can.
pages.mirrorMoon:
In that case, at least imagine it.
If it is an opponent you cannot match in real life, beat it in your imagination.
If you cannot beat it yourself, imagine something that you could beat it with.

pages.ja:
……そんな事、言われなくても判っている。
勝てるとしたら、それはこの頭の中でだけだろう。
だが、何を思えば勝てるのか。
俺は、衛宮士郎がサーヴァントを倒している姿なんて想像できない。
そこまで器用に自分を騙せないし、自分を騙して作ったイメージなんて所々にボロが出る。
そんな三流の想像で、一流の幻想であるサーヴァントに太刀打ち出来る筈がない。

pages.en:
…I know that without being told.

If I can win at all, it will only be here, within my own mind.

But what could I imagine that would grant me victory?

I cannot picture myself—Shirou Emiya—defeating a Servant.

I am not clever enough to deceive myself so completely, and any image born of such deception would be riddled with flaws.

A third-rate imagining like that could never contend with a Servant—a fantasy of the first order.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…He doesn’t need to tell me something I already know.
If I am going to win, it’ll only be in my head.
But what could I win with?
I can’t imagine myself beating a Servant.
I can’t handily deceive myself, and an image created by deceiving myself will be full of flaws.
There’s no way I would be able to match a Servant, a first-class illusion, with such a third rate image.

pages.ja:
だから。
俺は何に勝ち、
何で勝つのか。
その答えを、今もこうして探して

pages.en:
—And so.

What must I overcome?

What will I use to overcome it?

Even now, I continue searching for the answer——
pages.mirrorMoon:
So.
What will I be able to beat?
And what will I beat it with?
I am searching for the answer to that question

許されるのならば、それを手にしたいと思っただけ。

——Am I searching for it?

The golden sword.

That blade belongs to her alone.

It is not that I want it for myself.

I merely thought it beautiful.

And, if I might be forgiven for it, wished that I could hold it in my hands.

It’s a sword for her alone.
I don’t want it myself.
It’s just beautiful.
I just want to hold it in my hands, if it’s permitted.

…What a deplorable habit for an apprentice mage.

Because the only thing I can do is look inside an object, I indulge in dreams far beyond my station.

But—if it is only a dream, surely I may at least imagine it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Geez, it’s a bad habit for an amateur magus.

Butif this is a dream, I should be allowed to at least think about it.

有るモノに手を加えるのが強化なのだから、もとより無いモノに意味はない。

First, hypothesize the fundamental structure and reproduce its constituent materials.

…No. As I thought, the fundamentals of strengthening alone are not enough.

Strengthening alters something that already exists. It means nothing when there is nothing to begin with.

If I am to recall that sword, I must add more steps to the process.
pages.mirrorMoon:
First, I assume the basic structure and reproduce the composing material.
…Oh, the basic form from when I use the strengthening magic isn’t enough as I thought.
Strengthening is changing something that’s already there, so it’s meaningless with something that isn’t there at all.
So if I am to remember that sword, I have to put more effort into it.

pages.ja:
それは、基本よりもっと前。
“強化”の手順を教わる前の技法、切嗣に教わる前、自分なりに考えた無駄だらけの魔術工程。

—It lies even further back than the fundamentals.

A method from before I learned the procedure for strengthening—before Kiritsugu taught me anything. A useless, circuitous work of magecraft I devised for myself.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s well before the basics.
It’s the process full of waste that I came up with before Kiritsugu taught me how to use the strengthening magic.

ええと、それは確か

pages.jaRuby:

……………………………………………………………………………………

When I come to myself, I am somewhere utterly beyond imagining.

豪華な天蓋つきのベッドに、足首まで埋まりそうな毛足の長い絨毯。

pages.en:
“——Where am I——?”

It is not merely an unfamiliar room.

There is a magnificent four-poster bed and a deep-pile carpet that might swallow my feet to the ankles.

Nearby stands a stone fireplace, no mere ornament but burning even now to warm the room.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What is this place?”
This isn’t just some place I’ve never seen before.
It has a bed with a gorgeous canopy, and a long carpet that makes it look like you could sink to your ankles.
A stone fireplace that is not just decorative, but actually functional.

pages.ja:

慎二の家で洋館には慣れていたが、これはそういうレベルの部屋じゃない。
……こういう感想を口にするのは面はゆいが、まるで昔話に出てくるお城のようだった。

pages.en:
The patterns upon the walls are not wallpaper; they have been carved directly into the stone.

I thought Shinji's home had accustomed me to Western mansions, but this room belongs to another world entirely.

…It feels embarrassing even to put it this way, but this is like a castle from an old tale.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The patterns on the wall aren’t just wallpaper as they are actually engraved.
I’m used to mansions like Shinji’s house, but this is on a different level.
…It’s embarrassing to say, but this is like a castle you’d read about in fairy tales.

“Whoa——I'm tied up…!?”

My hazy thoughts clear in an instant.

Sensing danger, I begin by taking stock of my condition.
pages.mirrorMoon:

Realizing the danger I’m in, I study my situation first.

“…I've been put in a chair with my hands behind me. These aren't handcuffs… No, it's only rope around my wrists.”

The situation is less dire than I first imagined, but I still cannot move.

My body remains numb, and with my arms bound like this, I cannot even rise from the chair.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I’m sitting in a chair and my hands are behind my back… handcuffs… no, they’re just tied with rope.”
I’m not in the worst condition, but it makes no difference to the fact that I cannot move.
My body is still numb, and I can’t even get up with my hands tied.

“…How long has it been…? There's no clock, of course.”

Nothing in the room resembles one.

The window is——behind me.

I twist around as far as I can, but the curtains keep me from seeing outside clearly.

Even so, the sun has plainly gone down.

I met Illya early this morning, so at least half a day must have passed.

I met Illya in the morning, so that means at least half a day has passed.

Wherever I may be, I have to return to Saber as quickly as possible.

I can’t trouble her by letting her know I’ve been kidnapped.
